keyTerms.def: The science of making decisions in the presence of scarce resources; the study of how to direct resources in a way that most efficiently achieves a given goal.
A company's plan to create value in a marketplace; a plan to create and sustain a competitive advantage.
Learn how to apply economic concepts and principles to achieve superior profit performance for firms. STRAT 401 = conceptual foundations; STRAT 402 = analytical underpinnings and quantitative rigor.

Economics requires the analyst to be explicit about key elements; there is a clear linkage between conclusions and assumptions, which 'leaves an audit trail that allows one to distinguish between derived propositions and unsupported conjectures.'
'In this class, we are managers, not consumers.' (How would you feel about Netflix raising their price?)

Markets to Pursue (industry, product, geographic markets most attractive); Unique Value to Offer (cost or differentiation); Resources and Capabilities to Develop; Sustaining Advantage (barriers to imitation).

Level 1 No AI; 2 AI Planning; 3 AI Collaboration; 4 Full AI; 5 AI Exploration. Midterms = Level 1; pre-class quizzes = 'clarify, don't answer'; spreadsheets/in-class = Levels 2-3; group project = Level 4.
Explain (readings, videos), Demonstrate (quizzes, in-class exercises), Guide (assignments, solutions), Enable (group project, midterm exams).

examFacts: Two midterms in Canvas — 50% of grade; closed book, closed note, Testing Center
Exam average below 80% → comprehensive retake in finals week, capped at 80%
cases: Airline case: rank airports by cost per mile — Cincinnati 0.22 (1), Atlanta 0.20 (2), SLC 0.17 (3), Boston 0.14 (4), LA 0.12 (5); factors: affluence, business travelers, traffic, plane type, number/concentration of airlines, geography (S01 slides pp.60-67)
